### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via NavigationConfigSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39d611d4769a567cff55b3321a6a70f3cc32e2ba` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f6a8e9298232d6c7232586e9713f199767254d6d` — the merge of head `b68e955306bbb335ede90d65672f4bd44fcbefba` into base `39d611d4769a567cff55b3321a6a70f3cc32e2ba`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f6a8e9298232d6c7232586e9713f199767254d6d && git checkout f6a8e9298232d6c7232586e9713f199767254d6d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 39d611d4769a567cff55b3321a6a70f3cc32e2ba b68e955306bbb335ede90d65672f4bd44fcbefba && git checkout -B drift-repro 39d611d4769a567cff55b3321a6a70f3cc32e2ba && git merge --no-ff b68e955306bbb335ede90d65672f4bd44fcbefba

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39d611d4769a567cff55b3321a6a70f3cc32e2ba
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 39d611d4769a567cff55b3321a6a70f3cc32e2ba` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b17aa295a4bfecdd5c3c4d5e395f637438d17947`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/record-surface.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts + ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectDataPage.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/InterfaceListPage.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-view/src/recordSurface.ts, ui/packages/react/src/hooks/useNavigationOverlay.ts

Inputs read: card #36730 body and every comment (triage 7104562672, unlock 7113261613, claim 7228443977, os-dev report 7229291227, amendment 7229306962), PR #38055 body and its comments, the net diff `b4c99b8dd1...b17aa295a4` (19 files, +249/-30), and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read at the head, not reviewed: `recordDrawerContext.ts`, `objectViewRecordNavigation.ts`, `recordDrawerStack.tsx`, `objectViewRecordOverlay.tsx`, `console/AppContent.tsx`, `utils/recordFormNavigation.ts`, `components/src/custom/navigation-overlay.tsx`, `plugin-form/src/ModalForm.tsx`, `components/src/custom/mobile-dialog-content.tsx`.

The rest of the diff (the nine locale bundles, the two test files, `ui/e2e/toast-under-modal.spec.ts`, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; what this record says about them is under ① and ② only.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Published accept set: unchanged. Right.** `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` moves four comment lines inside the TSDoc block above `NavigationConfigSchema.width`; the schema expression and its `.describe()` string on the same key are byte-identical. `packages/spec/src/data/record-surface.ts` replaces a one-line TSDoc on `RecordFlowSurface.size`; the member's type `'auto' | 'full'` is unchanged. No key, enum value, default or `.describe()` text moves, so no JSON-schema or reference-doc output moves (the dev reports `check:generated` 14/14 up to date; the CI `Spec property liveness` run is green).
- **Published bytes: they do move. Right as declared.** Both spec edits are TSDoc on exported symbols and reach the `.d.ts`; so do the comment edits in `@object-ui/plugin-view` (`OverlaySize`, `deriveOverlaySize`, `overlayWidthFor`) and `@object-ui/react` (`resolveOverlayWidth`). The PR treats them as shipped bytes, not as skippable.
- **Public surface of the UI packages: unchanged. Right.** No export is added or dropped. `deriveOverlaySize` stays exported from `@object-ui/plugin-view`; at the head its only caller is `overlayWidthFor`, whose only caller is `recordPaneWidth` with a non-`auto` bucket.
- **Behaviour change (b): two drawers change their opening width and gain a drag handle. Right, and declared.** `/data` and the interface list page go from the overlay's 42rem with no `storageKey` to `min(92vw, 460px)` with a remembered width. Amendment 7229306962 and the PR's Acceptance notes both state the drag handle.
- **Locale leaves (a): nine strings change, no key added or dropped. Right.** One line per bundle. Each of ar, de, es-ES, fr, ja-JP, ko, pt-BR, ru and zh-Hant carries every clause of the unchanged en `.describe()` of `navigation.size` (fixed host default, same for every object whatever the field count, 460px in the console, the 480/720/960/1200/1600 caps clamped to the viewport, a dragged width wins over either, prefer it over pixel `width`, no effect where the record opens as a page or on a phone-width screen) and none carries the retired field-count or "AI writes nothing" clause. Nothing in them states a behaviour the head does not have; (b) makes the 460px clause true on two more console drawers.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: holds.** No authorable key, stored shape or wire shape moves.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` holds: the accept set is unchanged and nothing an author can write parses differently. The changeset is one file with five `patch` entries (`@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/plugin-view`, `@object-ui/react`), which is exactly the set of packages whose `src` moves. The comment-only spec, plugin-view and react edits take a patch and not `skip-changeset`, as the house rule requires for shipped TSDoc bytes. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The claim named three changesets; amendment 7229306962 adds the other two, so the claim and the diff agree.

Changeset prose, read against the head: the nine-locale paragraph, the 42rem and not-draggable statement for both drawers at the merge base, "at 460px, or at the width the reader last dragged in any side preview", and "an interface list page also takes its source view's `navigation.size` bucket, or its pixel `width`, which then wins over the shared dragged width" (an authored size or width moves the drawer to the per-object key, so the shared key is not read) are each true. The third paragraph's "now say what the code does" is true except for the one sentence under S1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in report 7229291227. Nothing to answer.
- Out-of-scope finding 1 (`deriveOverlaySize` still exported, no console caller for `auto`): confirmed at the head; the rewritten plugin-view comments say so truthfully. Removing a public export is not this card's. Accepted as noted.
- Out-of-scope finding 2 (`objectViewRecordNavigation` reads the off-spec `objectDef.navigation`): confirmed, untouched here. `InterfaceListPage` does not copy that read; it passes `viewDef?.navigation` only. Accepted as noted.
- Claim surface: 19 files against "about 15"; the extra ones are the new pin file and the two amended changeset entries. No file outside the claimed surface is touched.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no data read, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- CI on the head is not concluded. Green: `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Auto Label`, `filter`, both shard planners. Pending at the time of this record, named and not waited for: `Build Core`, `Build UI Deps`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test Core (1/10)` to `(10/10)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`. No run has failed. This record does not stand in for those verdicts.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/record-surface.ts` — `RecordFlowSurface.size`**

- "The record drawer's width does not read it (that is `navigation.size`'s)": true. Every drawer width at the head comes from `recordPaneWidth` (`recordDrawerContext.ts:132`) or `resolveOverlayWidth` (`useNavigationOverlay.ts:177`), which read `navigation.width` and `navigation.size` and nothing from the flow surface.
- "routes ignore it": true. The only reader of the derived `size` is `AppContent.tsx:1802`, for the create / edit dialog.
- "lets `'auto'` size itself": true. `resolveRecordFormModalLayout` (`recordFormNavigation.ts:232`) sets no `modalSize` for `'auto'`, and ModalForm then picks its own bounded `lg` / `xl`.
- S1 (should-fix) — "the console's create / edit dialog turns `'full'` into its full-screen sheet" is not what the code does. `resolveRecordFormModalLayout` turns a derived `'full'` into ModalForm's `modalSize: 'full'` (`recordFormNavigation.ts:240`), and that size is the class `sm:max-w-[95vw] sm:w-full` (`ModalForm.tsx:345`) with the common height `sm:h-auto sm:max-h-[90vh]`: a 95vw dialog from `sm` up, not a full-screen one. The full-screen sheet is ModalForm's below-`sm` posture (`mobile-dialog-content.tsx:135`, `fixed inset-0 ... h-[100dvh]`), which every size gets, `'auto'` included; ModalForm's own comment says so (`:331`). The console host also calls `deriveRecordFlowSurface` with no `viewport` (`AppContent.tsx:1802` and the comment above it), so it never receives `'full'` at all. The sentence is new, ships in the `.d.ts`, and card (c) asks that each comment say what the code does. A wording that holds: the console's create / edit dialog passes `'full'` to its form dialog as that dialog's `full` size (95vw from the `sm` breakpoint up; below it the dialog is a full-screen sheet whatever the size) and lets `'auto'` size itself.

**`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` — deprecated `NavigationConfig.width`**

- "It is still honoured": true. `recordPaneWidth` returns an authored `width` as written (`recordDrawerContext.ts:134`); `resolveOverlayWidth` returns it first (`useNavigationOverlay.ts:179`); the grid, kanban, calendar, gantt and tree overlays read the hook's resolved `width`; ObjectView's form drawer reads it (`ObjectView.tsx:2913`).
- "where a renderer reads both keys an authored `width` wins over `size` (the console's record drawer does)": true. Both resolvers that read both keys test `width` first. The console's record drawer goes through `recordPaneWidth` on all four hosts at the head: the object list (`objectViewRecordNavigation.ts:266`), the drawer stack (`recordDrawerStack.tsx:993`), and now `InterfaceListPage.tsx:739`; `/data` authors neither key.
- "so new metadata sets `size` (or omits it for `auto`) and leaves `width` out": agrees with the unchanged `.describe()` texts ("Prefer this over the pixel `width`" on `size`; "use the `size` bucket" on `width`). The TSDoc and the `.describe()` do not contradict each other; the TSDoc adds the precedence fact, which is the reason to leave `width` out.
- N1 (nit) — the unchanged `size` TSDoc three lines above glosses the console's 460px side panel as "(opened from an object's list, and the drawer level over a record page)". After (b) the `/data` drawer and the interface list page's drawer open at 460 as well, so the gloss is no longer the whole list. It is not false, and the `.describe()` text carries no such list. A follow-up may widen it.

**`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectDataPage.tsx`**

Agrees with the contract. The width is `RECORD_PREVIEW_DEFAULT_WIDTH` (`recordDrawerContext.ts:96`, `'min(92vw, 460px)'`), imported, not a new literal; it reaches the overlay through `resolveOverlayWidth`. The key is `RECORD_PREVIEW_WIDTH_KEY` (`'drawer-width:record-preview'`), the same constant `objectViewRecordOverlay.tsx:37` defaults to and `recordPreviewWidthKey` returns for an unauthored view. The page has no view, so there is no authored `size` to honour, as the claim says. The overlay enables resize only for a `storageKey` in drawer mode, which is the mode here; a remembered width is capped at 900 and the phone keeps the full-width sheet, so the help text's phone clause holds.

**`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/InterfaceListPage.tsx`**

Agrees with the contract. `width={recordPaneWidth(viewDef?.navigation, objectDef)}` follows the spread of the hook state, so it is the width the overlay draws: authored `width` first, then an authored bucket through `overlayWidthFor`, else the shared 460 default. `storageKey={recordPreviewWidthKey(cfg.source, viewDef?.navigation)}` is the shared key unless the source view authors a width or a non-`auto` size, then the per-object key, exactly as on the object list. Both names are in scope before the early return. Tried to break it: an `auto` or absent `navigation`, a hollow `viewDef` (undefined resolves to the default and the shared key), a `page` or `none` record action (the overlay is not drawn), and a phone (the sheet is full width regardless of the variable). None breaks.

**`ui/packages/plugin-view/src/recordSurface.ts`**

Each rewritten sentence is true at the head: `OverlaySize` is the five buckets other than `'auto'`; `deriveOverlaySize` is a field-count bucket that `auto` does not mean; `overlayWidthFor` falls back to it for `'auto'` or nothing, and the console never passes either because `recordPaneWidth:136` resolves `auto` first. No pairing with `FormView.modalSize` remains.

**`ui/packages/react/src/hooks/useNavigationOverlay.ts`**

True at the head: `resolveOverlayWidth` returns `width` first, then a bucket, and `undefined` for `'auto'` or absent, which is the host's own default. "The console's record hosts pass the side preview's fixed width as `width`" holds for the object list and `/data` through `navigation.width`, and for the drawer stack and the interface list page through the overlay's `width` prop.

Open on this head: S1 (should-fix), which earns a delta review of its fix. N1 is a nit. No must-fix.

  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's

  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/166e2125-4268-552f-a555-2b7c43a99f0f/scratchpad/pr-38055/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST

**L1 REWORK** at `b17aa295a4` (L1-a for the seat). The isolated `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record 7229399221 is a **PASS** (claim 7229329247, filled brief 7229411820, `verify-review-tier` PASS). It has no must-fix and one **should-fix**, which owes a delta of its fix.

**What holds.**
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are confirmed. The schema expressions and every `.describe()` string are byte-identical, so the accept set is unchanged. The comment-only spec edits ship in the `.d.ts`, so a patch changeset is right.

**Owed before ACCEPT.**
- **S1 (should-fix).** The new TSDoc on `RecordFlowSurface.size` (`packages/spec/src/data/record-surface.ts`) says "the console's create / edit dialog turns `'full'` into its full-screen sheet". The code does not do that:
  - A derived `'full'` becomes ModalForm's `modalSize: 'full'` (`recordFormNavigation.ts`), which is a 95vw dialog from `sm` up (`ModalForm.tsx`, height capped at 90vh), not full-screen.
  - The full-screen sheet is the below-`sm` posture that every size gets, `'auto'` included (`mobile-dialog-content.tsx`).
  - The console host also calls `deriveRecordFlowSurface` with no `viewport` (`AppContent.tsx`), so it never receives `'full'`.

  The sentence is new, ships in the `.d.ts`, and card part (c) asks that each comment say what the code does. The record offers a wording that holds: the console's create / edit dialog passes `'full'` to its form dialog as that dialog's `full` size (95vw from the `sm` breakpoint up; below it the dialog is a full-screen sheet whatever the size) and lets `'auto'` size itself.

  The changeset's "now say what the code does" inherits this, so fix both in the same push. The fix moves the head and owes a same-reviewer delta.

**Nit (not blocking).**
- N1: the unchanged `size` TSDoc in `view.zod.ts` lists where the console's 460 px panel opens. After (b), `/data` and the interface list page open at 460 px too, so the list is incomplete but not false. Take it in the same push or leave it as a follow-up.
